title: `key_range_auto()` double-transforms positions on transformed continuous scales
description: Hi, thanks for developing **legendry**. I think `key_range_auto()` currently applies scale transformations twice when used with transformed continuous position scales. I first encountered this with a `Date` x-axis, where `guide_axis_nested()` throws an error, but the issue appears to be more general and may also affect transformations such as `log10`, `sqrt`, and `reverse`. ### Date example ```r library(ggplot2) library(legendry) df <- data.frame( x = seq(as.Date("2025-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 24), y = seq_len(24) ) ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_line() + scale_x_date( date_breaks = "1 month", labels = function(x) format(x, "%b|%Y"), guide = guide_axis_nested() ) ``` ```text Error in `transform$transform()`: ! `transform_date()` works with objects of class only ``` This fails while the range key is being extracted. ### `sqrt` example The same issue seems to affect other transformed scales. For example: ```r df <- data.frame( x = c(1, 4, 9, 16), y = seq_len(4) ) ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + scale_x_sqrt( breaks = c(1, 4, 9, 16), labels = c("1|A", "4|A", "9|B", "16|B"), guide = guide_axis_nested() ) ``` Unlike the Date case, this may not necessarily throw an error, but the inferred range positions appear to be transformed twice. The same principle should apply to transformations such as `log10` and `reverse`. ### Suspected cause `range_from_label()` obtains a standard guide key using: https://github.com/teunbrand/legendry/blob/8fb52c042362b3ce95b946297a7ec914436dece0/R/key-range.R#L256 and then constructs the range positions from the first column: https://github.com/teunbrand/legendry/blob/8fb52c042362b3ce95b946297a7ec914436dece0/R/key-range.R#L292 For continuous position scales, these values appear to already be in transformed scale space. Later, `range_extract_key()` applies the scale transformation again: https://github.com/teunbrand/legendry/blob/8fb52c042362b3ce95b946297a7ec914436dece0/R/key-range.R#L180-L181 So conceptually, for a square-root scale: ```text data: 1 4 9 16 first transform: 1 2 3 4 second transform: 1 √2 √3 2 ``` For a Date scale the second transformation can fail because the transformed numeric positions are passed back to a Date transformation. Thanks!

``` r
    # Combine keys
    
    #### Drop the .group column
    new_params$key$.group <- new_params$key$.label <- new_params$key$.value <- NULL
    ####
    
    params$key <- vec_cbind(params$key, new_params$key)
    
    # Combine override.aes
    params$override.aes <- c(params$override.aes, new_params$override.aes)
    nms <- names(params$override.aes)
    if (anyDuplicated(nms)) {

    }
    params$override.aes <- params$override.aes[!duplicated(nms)]
    params$aesthetic <- union(params$aesthetic, new_params$aesthetic)
    
    list(guide = self, params = params)
  }
)
```

title: FR: Add dimension labels in `guide_legend_cross()`
description:
Hi, 

Here is an idea on specific, yet common cases: crossed comparisons.

For instance, one could imagine a plot for a diagnosis test, with matching cases being plain while non-matching cases being dimmed. 
The plot would have 2 colors (positive/negative) and 2 alphas (matching/ non-matching).
However, the default alpha legend is not very intuitive, and it would be much better IMHO if it could be "crossed".

An example is worth a thousand words, so here is a clumsy one using `patchwork`:

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
set.seed(0)

df = expand.grid(x=1:5, tag1 = c("+", "-"), tag2=c("+", "-")) %>% 
  mutate(y = runif(n()))

p = df %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = x, y = y, fill=tag1, group=tag1, alpha=tag1==tag2) +
  geom_col(position = 'dodge', show.legend=FALSE) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values=c(0.5, 1))

legend = df %>% 
  distinct(tag1, tag2) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = fct_rev(tag1), y = tag2, fill=fct_rev(tag1), group=tag1, alpha=tag1==tag2) +
  geom_tile(width=0.9, height=0.9, show.legend=FALSE) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values=c(0.5, 1)) + 
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x="Disease", y="Test") +
  theme_minimal()
  
wrap_plots(p, legend, widths=c(6,1))
```

title: `guide_axis_nested()` : `pad_discrete=0`
description:
Hi,

Thank you for this incredible package.

I'm building a rather large plot with a nested categorical x-axis.
My X labels are long and tend to overwrite each other, so I want to add a 30°angle on the top level.
However, this caused several alignment problems I couldn't solve using the available documentation.

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(legendry)

p = mpg |>
  filter(class %in% c("compact", "minivan")) |>
  mutate(cyl = str_replace(cyl, "4", "four"),
         cyl = str_replace(cyl, "5", "five"),
         cyl = str_replace(cyl, "6", "six"),

  ggplot() +

  geom_boxplot() +
```

```r
  )
```

With an angle on the top level, the alignment is OK, but the brackets shrink due to `pad_discrete=0`. 
Unfortunately, removing it causes the alignment to be very bad.

```r
levels_text = list(element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), 
                   element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1))

  guides(

  )
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b18a403-00e0-4b8f-8954-710f4ee4f22d)

Is there a way to get the best of the two worlds?

My first guess would be to state `pad_discrete=c(0, NA)` to have 0 for the top level and `waiver()` for the bottom level.

title: adding numbers at risk to survival curves
description:
I very much like the binning options for discrete axis guides, for example, and i wonder if more flexibility could be added (or is already available) for continuous axes. (I'm still tinkering with this package.)

As a motivating and illustrative example, i'd like to add a second guide for the abscissa of a survival plot that vertically juxtaposes each time label with a number-at-risk label for each cohort. I'm having trouble getting {reprex} to work, so below is the code and the three plots are added later. This works in a pinch, but it suffers from several problems:
1. A lot of guide preparation must be done manually; a tool that accepts a transformation and returns a new guide adapted from an existing guide would eliminate most of this.
2. In order to add a side title to the new guide but not to the existing guide, i must, it seems, use `compose_stack()` (3rd plot, compare to 2nd). Or can i add a side title using only `guide_axis_nested()`?
3. I was unable to position the new guide below the old label ("Years") rather than above it. Can this be done?

Perhaps this isn't the intended use case for this package! But it gets tantalizingly close, so it seems worth checking. Thank you so much for writing it!

```r
library(survival)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggfortify)
library(legendry)

# pre-process data
lung |> 
  subset(select = c(time, status, sex)) |> 
  transform(sex = ifelse(sex == 1, "male", "female")) ->
  lung_dat
head(lung_dat)

# fit Kaplan-Meier estimates
lung_fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + sex, data = lung_dat)
print(lung_fit)

# build survival curves
lung_fit |> 
  fortify() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = time / 365.2422, y = surv)) +
  geom_step(aes(color = strata)) +
  ggfortify:::geom_confint(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = strata),
    alpha = .25
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Surviving") ->
  lung_curve
print(lung_curve)

# tabulate numbers at risk
lung_fit |> 
  fortify() |> 
  subset(select = c(time, n.risk, strata)) |> 
  transform(interval = floor(time / 365.2422)) |> 
  split(~ strata + interval) |> 
  lapply(tail, n = 1L) |> 
  do.call(what = rbind) |> 
  transform(time = interval * 365.2422) ->
  lung_risk
print(lung_risk)
# tabulate value ranges
lung_range <- key_range_map(
  lung_risk,
  start = time / 365.2422, end = time / 365.2422, name = n.risk,
  hjust = 1
)
print(lung_range)

# annotate curves using a single {legendry} guide
lung_curve + 
  scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis_nested(
    regular_key = "auto", key = lung_range
  ))
# annotate curves using a composite {legendry} guide
lung_curve +
  guides(x = compose_stack(
    guide_axis_nested(
      regular_key = "auto", key = lung_range
    ),
```

title: guide_colbar title property adjustment
description:
Dear Teun van den Brand,

Can `guide_colbar` add `title.position` and `title.hjust` parameters to adjust the title position of the colorbar like guide_colorbar in ggplot?

The following code adjusts the position of the colorbar, the position of the colorbar header (**top and hjust**), but does not set the out-of-range triangle shape:
```
library(tidyverse)
library(legendry)
library(terra)

m <- matrix(1:25, nrow=5, ncol=5)
rm <- rast(m)

# from a "xyz" data.frame
data <- as.data.frame(rm, xy=TRUE)
bwr_colors <- c("blue", "white", "red")

ggplot(data = data,aes(x = x,y = y,fill = lyr.1)) +
  geom_tile() + 
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = bwr_colors, 
    na.value = NA,
    limits = c(5, 20), oob = scales::oob_squish,
    guide = guide_colorbar(#shape = "triangle",
                         title.position = "top",
                         title.hjust = 0.5)) +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",             
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),       
    legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"))
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/139ea88a-1230-4aa8-b09d-abadb2979d3c)


It's more elegant to use `guide_colbar` when setting the triangle shape, but it doesn't seem to be possible to set the title position of the colorbar: 
```
ggplot(data = data,aes(x = x,y = y,fill = lyr.1)) +
  geom_tile() + 
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = bwr_colors, 
    na.value = NA,
    limits = c(5, 20), oob = scales::oob_squish,
    guide = guide_colbar(shape = "triangle")
                         # title.position = "top",
                         # title.hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",             
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),       
    legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"))     
)
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf7e7d1a-8d61-45a4-a70c-ca8ea0dd47c1)

If settings similar to the above are made, an error is prompted: 
```
`Error in guide_colbar(shape = "triangle", title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5) : 
  unused arguments (title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)'
```

Best regards
Hu
